summary: Olivia Chow's public posts on civic engagement emphasize broad participation in democratic life, community organizing, and direct consultation with affected residents. Chow repeatedly encourages voting, including early voting and voting based on conviction rather than fear (uGINR0utA2, t-5vGnutPZ, pJp-RlutGb, CtUbO-FgORx), and frames democracy as strengthened by exchange of ideas (CuAqVppPbav). Chow highlights systemic barriers to younger voters' engagement and the need to meet them on social media (Cst4qC_JZ4B), and recognizes working people, volunteers, and faith-community organizations as builders of a more equitable city (Csrr8tmPhyK, rfmY9OOtJG, Cr9ZV3pvq-u). Chow describes consulting Flemingdon families on the Science Centre and standing with workers and residents (CrPADE5p7N1, Cr9aUuAtQRF), expresses solidarity with Pride and Sikh communities (Ct422Chv9qe, Ct2rNF5NJRl), and pledges to listen and learn from Torontonians as Mayor (CrqpZEkgbe7).

key_positions.stance: Encourages broad voter participation, including early voting and voting based on conviction
Frames democracy as strengthened by lively exchange of ideas and people demanding better
Identifies systemic barriers to younger generations' political engagement and calls on candidates to meet them on social media
Recognizes working people, volunteers, and community organizations as central to building a more equitable Toronto
Expresses solidarity with marginalized and diaspora communities, including 2SLGBTQI+ and Sikh communities
Supports cultural and community spaces in neighbourhoods outside the downtown core
Values direct consultation with affected residents on civic decisions

key_actions.action: Cast a ballot in early voting in the Toronto mayoral by-election
Consulted Flemingdon families about the future of the Ontario Science Centre and stood with OPSEU/SEFPO workers and residents to oppose its relocation
Presented the 2023 Mayor's Purchase Awards at the Toronto Outdoor Art Fair
Presented the first Jack Layton Progress Prize to Fay Blaney of the Women's Memorial March Committee
Joined a rally with Spadina–Fort York residents and NDP colleagues to oppose Bill C-51
Participated in a large canvass focused on women's issues in Spadina–Fort York
Pledged, as Mayor, to listen and learn from Torontonians and act to make their lives easier
